newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Former bank governor to lead Yugoslav opposition.
newsitem.headline: Former bank governor to lead Yugoslav opposition.

text.p: Former Yugoslav central bank governor Dragoslav Avramovic has agreed to head an opposition coalition in November elections, an opposition spokesman said on Friday.

Slobodan Vuksanovic, spokesman for the opposition coalition Zajedno (Together) said Avramovic would lead them in Yugoslav parliamentary elections scheduled for November 3, adding that the former bank chief would formally announce his candidacy at a news conference on Saturday.
The Zajedno coalition includes the Serbian Renewal Movement, The Civic Alliance of Serbia and the Democratic Party -- three of Yugoslavia's main opposition parties.
As National Bank governor Avramovic won wide public respect for his tight-money policies, credited for reigning in hyperinflation of 60 percent a day in January 1994 and stabilising the economy.

But in May this year the Yugoslav government sacked him following a dispute over negotiations with international monetary institutions to restore the country's financial ties after four years of sanctions.
The government disagreed with his support for rapid liberalisation and privatisation of the centrally-regulated economy.

Soon after his dismissal, Avramovic backed striking workers demanding unpaid wages from state companies, and reduced taxes. Then he accepted an invitation to join a trade union think-tank on economic and political reform.
Diplomats and political analysts said Avramovic and his coalition was unlikely to beat the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) which maintains a tight grip over most of the country's media.
Questions are also likely to arise over Avramovic's health. Last December, he went to hospital for kidney problems and heart weakness, and took almost a month off work.
